entries.effect: NO, and it is the whole of the property on this release: NSTextList.h:65 of the 26.2 SDK declares `@property (readonly, class) BOOL includesTextListMarkers` and documents it as "When YES, TextKit includes text list marker in the contents. It is NO by default", and a list is nothing but its markers while the port's text system produces no marker at all - NSTextListMarker is not a class the port carries, only its seventeen enumerated constants are (registry/UIKit/measured-constants.json) - so there is no text whose contents could hold one. The accessor is the CLASS method +includesTextListMarkers and there is no setter, because Apple's class has neither an instance accessor nor one
entries.source: SDK 26.2 surface, UIKit (via=own). The port's own object is packages/a/apple-backports/UIKit/UIKit26_0.m, category NSTextList (RevenantUIKit26), which defines +includesTextListMarkers and nothing else of this name. Measured on Apple's own class, the arm64e shared cache of iOS 18.0 read with modules/apple/objc.lua's inventory: includesTextListMarkers is in NSTextList's METACLASS list and in neither of its instance lists. Measured on the host's own class, one process and the same probe twice, the only difference being whether the port's object is linked: with it NOT linked, +includesTextListMarkers answers NO and -includesTextListMarkers and -setIncludesTextListMarkers: are both absent; with it linked, all three read the same, which is what the earlier instance getter and setter here used to change. Read out of the compiled object, otool -v -s __TEXT __objc_methname on UIKit26_0.o carries the one selector includesTextListMarkers. No header declares a getter for the property, which is why the surface's getter column is empty for this row

entries.effect: BOTH ACCESSORS ARE EXPORTED and the getter answers BOOL, because the SDK declares this a readwrite property and not a method: UIViewPropertyAnimator.h:49 reads `@property(nonatomic) BOOL flushUpdates`, so an application that writes `animator.flushUpdates = YES` sends setFlushUpdates: and one that reads it sends flushUpdates. The object defined `- (void)flushUpdates` before this commit, which answered neither -- the write raised unrecognized selector setFlushUpdates: and the read returned whatever was in the return register. What the pair holds is the honest nothing: the 16.4 SDK's UIViewPropertyAnimator declares no flush and no updateEverything, so there is nothing to forward to, the getter returns NO until a setter stores otherwise, and a 6.1.3 animator runs its animations without the 26.0 flush-on-every-context-change
